proposals.citation: Wang K, Takahashi Y, Gao ZL, Wang GX, Chen XW, Goto J, Lou JN, Tsuji S. Mitochondrial ND3 as the novel causative gene for Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia. Neurogenetics 10: 337-45, 2009. [PubMed: 19458970]
proposals.label: Wang et al. (2009)
proposals.rationale: Wang et al. (2009) give the first evidence that MT-ND3 causes LDYT: a homoplasmic m.10197G>A (Ala47Thr) mutation in a Chinese family with 18 affected members. Until now the entry's evidence covered only MT-ND4 and MT-ND6 variants. The paper also notes that the same mutation causes Leigh syndrome, which links the two phenotypes.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2009) described a Chinese family with 18 patients affected by Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia, in whom vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia occurred in variable combinations.

paragraphs.text: LDYT, an oxidative phosphorylation disorder, had previously been attributed to mutations in the mitochondrial ND6 and ND4 genes. Wang et al. (2009) found a mutation in the MT-ND3 gene in a family with LDYT, which added a further causative gene.

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese family with LDYT, Wang et al. (2009) used resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome and identified an m.10197G-A transition in the MT-ND3 gene. The mutation caused an ala47-to-thr (A47T) substitution at a highly conserved residue and occurred on a haplogroup D4b background. Quantitative heteroplasmy analysis showed that the mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. The authors stated that this was the first ND3 mutation reported to cause LDYT.

proposals.label: Spruijt et al. (2007)
proposals.rationale: The paper is the first in the evidence to report a patient variant in MT-ND1. The existing evidence has variants only in MT-ND4 and MT-ND6. It reports the 3697G-A mutation in a family with both LHON and spastic dystonia, with isolated complex I deficiency. It also notes that the same mutation can cause MELAS, which suggests other genetic factors affect how the disease is expressed.

proposals.label: McFarland et al. (2007)
proposals.rationale: The paper reports 2 new families in which dystonia was the main manifestation and epilepsy was also present. One family carried a heteroplasmic m.11778G>A MT-ND4 mutation at very high levels; this variant is not in the variant table. The other carried a new homoplasmic mutation in mitochondrial tRNA(Cys) (MTTC), a gene not currently linked to the entry. Epilepsy is not among the clinical features already listed.

paragraphs.text: McFarland et al. (2007) reported 6 patients from 2 families in whom dystonia was the principal clinical manifestation. A mitochondrial cause was considered because the dystonia occurred with other, less prominent features such as epilepsy. The authors advocated considering mitochondrial disease in patients with familial, progressive dystonia, particularly when additional neurologic features such as epilepsy are present.

proposals.citation: Watanabe M, Mita S, Takita T, Goto Y, Uchino M, Imamura S. Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy with dystonia in a Japanese family. J Neurol Sci 243: 31-4, 2006. [PubMed: 16380132]
proposals.label: Watanabe et al. (2006)
proposals.rationale: Watanabe et al. (2006) found the m.14459G>A variant in MT-ND6, which the entry already lists, in the first Japanese family with LHON and dystonia shown to carry an mtDNA mutation. The variant was absent from 200 Japanese controls. The paper also describes the course in this family: generalized dystonia beginning in childhood and optic neuropathy beginning later in life. These findings extend what is known about the variant's ethnic distribution but do not change the entry's core facts.

paragraphs.text: Watanabe et al. (2006) described a Japanese family in which affected members had generalized dystonia, attributed to striatal degeneration, beginning in childhood, and optic neuropathy beginning later in life.

paragraphs.text: In the proband from a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia, Watanabe et al. (2006) sequenced the entire mtDNA and identified 42 nucleotide changes compared with the revised Cambridge Reference Sequence. These changes included the G14459A mutation in the MT-ND6 gene, which was not present in 200 healthy Japanese controls. The authors noted that this mutation had previously been suggested as the cause of LHON and/or dystonia in Hispanic, African American, and Caucasian families. They reported this as the first Japanese family with LHON and dystonia in which an mtDNA mutation had been found. The proband also carried an A3203G change, which was not present in 200 healthy Japanese controls; its significance remained unknown.

evidence.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) described a Japanese family in which affected members had generalized dystonia, attributed to striatal degeneration, beginning in childhood, and optic neuropathy beginning later in life.
quotes: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.

evidence.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) sequenced the entire mtDNA of the proband from a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia and found 42 nucleotide changes compared with the revised Cambridge Reference Sequence. These included the G14459A mutation in the ND6 gene (MT-ND6), which was absent from 200 healthy Japanese controls. The authors noted that this mutation had previously been suggested as the cause of LHON and/or dystonia in Hispanic, African American, and Caucasian families, and they reported this as the first Japanese family with LHON and dystonia in which an mtDNA mutation was found.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.

The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
To our knowledge, this is the first case of LHON with dystonia that revealed a mtDNA mutation in a Japanese family.

evidence.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) also found an A3203G change in the proband's mtDNA. This change was absent from 200 healthy Japanese controls, and the authors stated that its significance remained unknown.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.
The significance of the A3203G mutation remains unknown.
